reviewed_finding: Mined external Symmetry.lean (FullyInvariantPoint, no_fully_invariant_point: a general swap argument, not vacuous; no selection-function type or equivariance notion exists in it) and the local DAG witness pg_collapse_barrier_protected_questions_and_l1_kkt_trace_embed, which is a fixed instance and partly vacuous (a constant function, the swap on Fin 2, unrelated KKT arithmetic). The ledger D01 definition of the asymmetry-price frontier has no Lean/Rust declaration; it is modelled here by the pointwise stabiliser of a declared set, which is a modelling choice with a different quantifier pattern from D01 (minimal declarations producing invariance versus minimal input sets whose removal frees a symmetry). The node proves the general theorem and the frontier characterisation in Lean and replays exact tables for carriers of size 0..6 with a brute-force permutation checker. The bottleneck WDP-CH03-P03 (declare-then-assert one-item separation) stays unported.

claim_boundary.supports: Over an arbitrary type X (Lean, general; the cardinality statement frontier_card is informative only for finite X, frontierEquiv and minimalSelecting_iff_singleton carry the general content): no point is fixed by every permutation when X has two distinct points (the bare-set form of "no Sym(X)-equivariant distinguished-point selection"); a point is invariant under the pointwise stabiliser of a declared set S iff it lies in S or the complement of S is that single point; S selects some point iff S is nonempty or X has exactly one point; for X with two distinct points the inclusion-minimal selecting sets are exactly the singletons, one per point (a consequence of the pointwise-stabiliser definition: a declared point is fixed because it is declared); on a one-point carrier the empty declaration already selects and on an empty carrier nothing does. Replay bound (not part of the Lean claim): exact tables for every subset of every carrier of size 0..6 (127 subsets), invariant points by enumerating all permutations fixing S, and the minimal selecting sets.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Retention, dynamics or observers being impossible or available (WDP-CH03-N01 is a nonclaim, not formalised); that Selecting / MinimalSelecting formalises WDP-CH03-D01 (D01 minimises declared input sets whose removal restores a symmetry that moves the output, relative to an implementation class and dependency preorder; here the minimal declarations making some point invariant under the pointwise stabiliser are computed, and the two agree on singletons only because the output is the declared point); a Lean notion of equivariant selection function (no_fully_invariant_point is its bare-set specialisation); the price of selection on structured carriers (rigid, cyclic, graph) or under the setwise stabiliser; WDP-CH03-P03; infinite-carrier cardinality; any physical or interpretive claim.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: On a bare set of at least two points no point is invariant under all permutations, and in the pointwise-stabiliser model the minimal selecting declarations are exactly the single declared points (price one declared point; price zero on a one-point carrier; no selection on the empty carrier); symmetry-price bookkeeping only.
claim_boundary.next_test: On structured carriers compute the same selecting and minimal tables with Sym(X) replaced by an explicit automorphism group G (n-cycle with rotations, K4 graph with its automorphisms, a rigid carrier with trivial G) and test whether the frontier is still the singletons: a rigid carrier must give price 0 and the n-cycle with rotations price 1; any other value falsifies the claim that the singleton frontier is generic.

second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T175809Z_staged. Lean (WdpProtectedQuestions.lean) states what the profile says: no_fully_invariant_point (any Nontrivial type, swap argument), invariantUnder_iff (x invariant under the pointwise stabiliser of S iff x in S or every point outside S equals x), selecting_iff (S selects iff nonempty or X has exactly one point), selecting_iff_nonempty, minimalSelecting_iff_singleton and frontierEquiv (X equivalent to the subtype of minimal selecting sets, valid for infinite X), frontier_card (informative for finite X only, now labelled), one_point_empty_selects, empty_carrier_no_selection, bool_instance. The header and profile now say plainly that the singleton frontier is a near-consequence of the pointwise-stabiliser modelling choice (first disjunct of invariantUnder_iff: a declared point is fixed because it is declared), that Selecting/MinimalSelecting is not ledger D01, and that no equivariant-selection-function type is defined. Checker: independent (all n! permutations per subset, minimality from the definition over proper subsets, producer uses a closed form), strict types incl. bool vs int in the table, public cases asserted to be exactly [0..6], min_price null for the empty carrier, theorem-level checks (empty declaration never selects, frontier = singletons for n>=2). Earlier pass (a): all five amendments are in the final text (singleton-frontier-is-definitional remark, frontier_card caveat, D01 non-identification and the selection-function non-claim in does_not_support, narrowest_claim rewritten without 'selection is not free', concrete next_test with rigid carrier price 0 and n-cycle price 1), the two missing near misses (setwise stabiliser, rigid carrier) were added (9 semantic mutants), and the sentinel -1 became null. (b) No weakening or new overclaim; the 127-subset replay bound is explicitly 'not part of the Lean claim'. (c) Residual issues: (1) the DAG statement's second sentence ('the asymmetry-price frontier is the family of inclusion-minimal declared input sets restoring the symmetry') is the D01 definition, which this node does not formalise; the node proves a characterisation in the pointwise-stabiliser model, so the DAG text must be narrowed (not the status: the first sentence, no fixed point on a bare set, is genuinely proved and more general than the external Fintype version). (2) The DAG Lean list still names pg_collapse_barrier_protected_questions_and_l1_kkt_trace_embed, which the profile correctly reads as a fixed, partly vacuous instance unrelated to the claim; it should not count as support. (3) The setwise_stabiliser_table mutant rationale says 'declared points are no longer invariant'; that holds only for |S| >= 2 (for a singleton S the setwise and pointwise stabilisers coincide and the declared point stays invariant). I recomputed the n=3 setwise table {0:0,1:1,2:2,3:4,4:4,5:2,6:1,7:0}; it is right, only the sentence is loose. Cosmetic. (4) The one-line reading 'no Sym(X)-equivariant distinguished-point selection = no point fixed by all permutations' is right for a selection with no input on a bare set; the profile says this is a specialisation. (5) P03 (declare-then-assert one-item separation) remains unported and is correctly in does_not_support and the DAG bottleneck, no longer duplicated in next_test.

dag_suggestion.statement: On an unstructured set with at least two elements no point is fixed by every permutation (the bare-set form of: no Sym(X)-equivariant distinguished-point selection exists). In the pointwise-stabiliser model, in which a declared input set is fixed pointwise, the inclusion-minimal declarations that make some point invariant are exactly the singletons (price one declared point; price zero on a one-point carrier; no selection on the empty carrier). The ledger definition D01 of the asymmetry-price frontier relative to an implementation class and dependency preorder is not formalised. The result says selection is not free on a bare set; it does not say retention or observers cannot exist.

earlier_pass.notes: The Lean anchors state what supports says: no_fully_invariant_point (any type with two distinct points; it is more general than the external Symmetry.lean version, which needs Fintype), invariantUnder_iff, selecting_iff, selecting_iff_nonempty, minimalSelecting_iff_singleton, one_point_empty_selects, empty_carrier_no_selection and bool_instance all check by hand. The checker really is a second computation (all n! permutations, minimality from the definition over proper subsets) against a closed-form producer, with strict types and a theorem-level check that the frontier is the singletons for n >= 2. The weaknesses are about meaning. (1) The frontier result is a consequence of the modelling choice, almost a tautology: in invariantUnder_iff the disjunct 'x in S' is closed by hsigma x hxS, i.e. a declared point is fixed because declaring means fixing it. So 'the frontier is the n singletons, price 1' says only that to select a point you must declare it; nothing about an implementation class, a dependency preorder, or what a non-bare carrier would cost. The claim boundary calls it a modelling choice, but narrowest_claim ('selection is not free') leans on it. (2) The ledger definition D01 (claim ledger line 60) is 'inclusion-minimal declared input sets, relative to a specified implementation class and dependency preorder, whose removal restores a symmetry that moves the output'. The model's Selecting/MinimalSelecting (minimal S that makes some point Stab(S)-invariant) is a different quantifier pattern: minimal declarations producing invariance versus minimal input sets whose removal frees a symmetry. They coincide numerically here because the output is the declared point; the profile only says the model is 'narrower', which understates the difference. (3) The DAG phrase 'no Sym(X)-equivariant distinguished-point selection' is rendered as 'no point fixed by all permutations'; that is the right reading for a selection with no input on a bare set, but no selection-function type or equivariance notion is defined in Lean. (4) frontier_card: Nat.card {S // MinimalSelecting S} = Nat.card X is 0 = 0 for an infinite carrier, so 'one per point' for 'an arbitrary type' is carried by minimalSelecting_iff_singleton, not by frontier_card; state it as an Equiv or restrict to finite X. (5) The checker never asserts that the public cases are exactly 0..6 (127 subsets claimed), and encodes 'nothing selects' as min_price = -1. Mutants: seven genuine misreadings (empty declaration selects, complement singleton ignored, rigidification price, non-minimal marked minimal, one-point and empty-carrier boundaries, price zero at five points), all single-record edits that recomputation rejects. Missing and important: the setwise-versus-pointwise stabiliser reading (for n = 3, S = {0,1}: pointwise gives invariant mask 7, setwise gives only point 2), which is the modelling choice the profile itself flags as 'narrower than D01'; and a rigid-carrier reading (trivial symmetry group, price 0), which would falsify 'the frontier is always the singletons' outside the bare-set model. next_test is partly the DAG bottleneck (P03 port: legitimate and node-owned) but both halves are listed in does_not_support, and 'redo the frontier with an explicit implementation class and dependency preorder' is a design task, not a test; a concrete falsifier is available (see amendments). DAG: P01 is genuinely proved (status PROVED_LEAN fine for that sentence), the frontier sentence is a definition plus a model; narrow it rather than lower the status.
